after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{8}{7} \\ -\frac{17}{7}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{8}{7} \\ -\frac{17}{7}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=3\sqrt{3}.
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}=10 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=5\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & 5 \\ 5 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}30 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 \\ -5 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}30 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}=10 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=5\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & 5 \\ 5 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}30 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 \\ -5 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}30 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=7 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-4\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 7 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 7 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 14 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 28 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{84}[\begin{aligned}21 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 28 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=\sqrt{21}.
$$
